_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Ethiopia covering Lucy/Australopithecus, Aksum and the Ark of the Covenant, Zagwe dynasty and Lalibela, Solomonic dynasty, Adwa victory, Haile Selassie, Italian occupation, Derg/Red Terror, EPRDF, Abiy Ahmed, and the Tigray War.

ethnic_groups.name: Oromo
ethnic_groups.notes: Largest ethnic group; Cushitic-speaking; Oromia region; historically Gada democratic system; include Borana, Arsi, Guji, Shewa clans

ethnic_groups.name: Amhara
ethnic_groups.notes: Semitic-speaking; historically dominant politically; Amhara region; Solomonic dynasty; Amharic language

ethnic_groups.name: Somali
ethnic_groups.notes: Ogaden/Somali Region; pastoralists; clan-based (Darod, Hawiye, Dir); 1977 Ogaden War

ethnic_groups.name: Tigray/Tigrayan
ethnic_groups.notes: Northern Ethiopia; Tigrinya-speaking; Aksumite heritage; TPLF dominance 1991–2018; Tigray War 2020–2022

ethnic_groups.name: Sidama
ethnic_groups.notes: Rift Valley; Cushitic; became autonomous region 2020; Sidama coffee

ethnic_groups.name: Gurage
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Ethiopia; Semitic-speaking; multiple sub-groups; known for trade and commerce

ethnic_groups.name: Welayta
ethnic_groups.notes: SNNPR; Omotic-speaking; historic Welayta Kingdom; seeking regional statehood

ethnic_groups.name: Afar
ethnic_groups.notes: Afar Region; Cushitic pastoralists; Danakil Depression; Sultanate of Aussa; cross-border with Djibouti/Eritrea

ethnic_groups.name: Other (80+ groups)
ethnic_groups.notes: Ethiopia has 80+ ethnic groups; Anuak, Nuer, Bench, Konso, Dorze, Hamer, Mursi, Surma and many others; extreme linguistic diversity

independence.notes: One of only two African nations never colonised (with Liberia); Italian occupation 1936–1941 not internationally recognised as colonisation

natural_resources.notes: Birthplace of coffee (Kaffa region, legend of goat herder Kaldi); second-largest African population; Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) on Blue Nile—Africa's largest, 6.45GW, Egypt-Sudan dispute; potential lithium deposits; teff grain unique to Ethiopia; flower exports #2 globally

military.notes: Ethiopian National Defense Force; Tigray War 2020-22 (estimated 600k-800k dead, one of deadliest 21st century conflicts); Eritrean forces involved; Amhara/Fano militia; Oromia OLF-Shane insurgency; AU peacekeeping contributor (AMISOM/ATMIS in Somalia)

climate_zones: Tropical highland (central, cool due to elevation 2,000-3,000m)

debt_aid.notes: Largest aid recipient in Africa; Chinese Belt & Road loans (Addis-Djibouti railway); 2023 debt restructuring under G20 Common Framework agreement; Ethiopian Airlines revenue critical; forex crisis severe

education.notes: Amharic instruction (primary) but transition to regional languages; university expansion (40+ public universities built since 2000); medical school expansion; ethnic federalism affects education language policy; UNESCO Learning Poverty ~90%

diaspora_migration.diaspora_population: 3.0 million (USA ~300k, Saudi Arabia, Israel, South Africa, UAE, Europe)
diaspora_migration.notes: Africa's largest refugee-hosting country (South Sudanese, Somalis, Eritreans); Tigray War created 2M+ IDPs; Ethiopian Jews (Beta Israel) airlifted to Israel (Operations Moses/Solomon); diaspora remittances critical; Washington DC largest Ethiopian community outside Africa

digital_economy.notes: Ethio Telecom monopoly broken 2022 (Safaricom Ethiopia launched); Telebirr mobile money massively adopted; internet shutdowns during conflicts; Hawassa Industrial Park for textile/tech; growing startup scene; digital ID system (Fayda) rolling out

current_leader.name: Abiy Ahmed
current_leader.title: Prime Minister
current_leader.notes: Oromo leader; Nobel Peace Prize 2019 for Eritrea peace; Prosperity Party; oversaw Tigray War 2020–2022

former_leaders.name: Emperor Haile Selassie I
former_leaders.notes: Last emperor; Solomonic dynasty; Pan-Africanist; OAU founder; Rastafari icon; overthrown by Derg

former_leaders.name: Mengistu Haile Mariam
former_leaders.notes: Derg military junta chairman; Red Terror; Ethiopian famine 1983–85; overthrown by EPRDF; exile in Zimbabwe

former_leaders.name: Meles Zenawi
former_leaders.notes: TPLF/EPRDF leader; President 1991–1995, PM 1995–2012; ethnic federalism architect; died in office

former_leaders.name: Hailemariam Desalegn
former_leaders.notes: SNNPR (Wolayta); first non-Tigray PM under EPRDF; resigned amid Oromo/Amhara protests

910.name: Cradle of Humanity
910.description: Ethiopia's Afar Triangle as one of the most important paleoanthropological sites on Earth; discovery of Australopithecus afarensis (Lucy) and other hominid fossils.

sub_clusters.name: Lucy and Australopithecus afarensis
sub_clusters.description: Discovery of 'Lucy' (Dinkinesh) in Hadar 1974; 3.2-million-year-old Australopithecus afarensis; bipedalism evidence.

sub_clusters.name: Omo and Herto: Earliest Homo sapiens
sub_clusters.description: Omo Kibish and Herto fossils — among oldest anatomically modern human remains; Ethiopia as origin point for Homo sapiens.

910.name: Ancient Ethiopian Civilisations
910.description: From the Land of Punt through D'mt kingdom to the Aksumite Empire; one of Africa's greatest ancient civilisations.

sub_clusters.name: Land of Punt Connections
sub_clusters.description: Ethiopian region as possible location of Punt; Egyptian trade expeditions for incense, gold, and exotic animals.

sub_clusters.name: D'mt Kingdom
sub_clusters.description: Pre-Aksumite kingdom in northern Ethiopia/Eritrea; Yeha temple; Sabaean cultural influences; proto-Ge'ez inscriptions.

sub_clusters.name: Aksumite Empire
sub_clusters.description: One of the four great powers of the ancient world; Aksum obelisks; King Ezana's conversion to Christianity c. 330; coinage; trade with Rome and India.

sub_clusters.name: Ark of the Covenant Tradition
sub_clusters.description: Ethiopian tradition of the Ark of the Covenant brought by Menelik I, son of Solomon and Queen of Sheba; Axum Tsion Church.

920.name: Zagwe and Solomonic Dynasties
920.description: Zagwe dynasty and the rock-hewn churches of Lalibela; Solomonic dynasty restoration; medieval Ethiopian Christianity; Prester John legend.

sub_clusters.name: Zagwe Dynasty and Lalibela Churches
sub_clusters.description: Zagwe dynasty rules from Roha (Lalibela); King Lalibela commissions eleven rock-hewn churches — 'New Jerusalem'; UNESCO World Heritage.

sub_clusters.name: Solomonic Dynasty Restoration
sub_clusters.description: Yekuno Amlak restores Solomonic dynasty 1270; Kebra Nagast legitimises lineage; Zara Yaqob's centralisation and religious reforms.

sub_clusters.name: Ethiopian–Adal Wars
sub_clusters.description: Ahmed Gran (Ahmad ibn Ibrahim) devastates Christian Ethiopia; Portuguese intervention; Battle of Wayna Daga 1543 restores Christian rule.

930.name: Gondar Period and Era of Princes
930.description: Gondar as capital; Fasilides' castles; Oromo expansion; Zemene Mesafint (Era of Princes) — decentralisation and warlordism.

sub_clusters.name: Gondar and Fasilides' Castles
sub_clusters.description: Emperor Fasilides founds Gondar 1636; castle complex; Jesuit expulsion; brief cultural flourishing.

sub_clusters.name: Oromo Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Massive Oromo migrations reshape Ethiopian demographics and politics; gadaa governance system; integration into imperial structures.

sub_clusters.name: Zemene Mesafint (Era of Princes)
sub_clusters.description: Period of weak emperors controlled by regional warlords (ras); fragmentation; Yejju Oromo dominance at Gondar.

940.name: Modern Ethiopian Empire
940.description: Tewodros II reunifies Ethiopia; Menelik II's expansion and Adwa victory; Haile Selassie's early reign and modernisation.

sub_clusters.name: Tewodros II and Yohannes IV
sub_clusters.description: Tewodros II ends Era of Princes; modernisation attempts; British Expedition to Magdala 1868; Yohannes IV's consolidation and battles with Egypt and Mahdist Sudan.

sub_clusters.name: Menelik II and the Battle of Adwa
sub_clusters.description: Menelik II expands Ethiopian borders; Treaty of Wuchale dispute; decisive victory at Battle of Adwa 1 March 1896 — Ethiopia remains unconquered.

sub_clusters.name: Haile Selassie's Rise and Modernisation
sub_clusters.description: Ras Tafari Makonnen becomes regent then Emperor Haile Selassie I 1930; 1931 constitution; League of Nations membership; Rastafari movement.

sub_clusters.name: Italian Invasion and Occupation
sub_clusters.description: Mussolini invades October 1935; Haile Selassie appeals to League of Nations; Italian East Africa; Yekatit 12 massacre 1937; British liberation 1941.

950.name: Haile Selassie's Imperial Era
950.description: Restoration of Haile Selassie; federation and annexation of Eritrea; founding of OAU in Addis Ababa; growing discontent.

sub_clusters.name: Post-Liberation Restoration
sub_clusters.description: Haile Selassie restored; modernisation efforts; Addis Ababa as capital of OAU (founded 1963); federation with Eritrea 1952.

sub_clusters.name: Ethiopian Revolution of 1974
sub_clusters.description: Wollo famine; student protests; military mutiny; Haile Selassie deposed 12 September 1974 by the Derg.

950.name: Derg Regime and Red Terror
950.description: Mengistu Haile Mariam's Marxist military junta; Red Terror; Ogaden War; famine 1984; fall to EPRDF coalition.

sub_clusters.name: Red Terror Campaign
sub_clusters.description: Mengistu's campaign of mass murder against political opponents; estimated tens of thousands killed; MEISON and EPRP targeted.

sub_clusters.name: Ogaden War with Somalia
sub_clusters.description: Somalia invades Ogaden; Soviet and Cuban intervention saves Ethiopia; Cold War proxy conflict.

sub_clusters.name: 1984 Famine and Live Aid
sub_clusters.description: Devastating famine kills ~400,000; BBC reporting sparks global response; Live Aid concert 1985; resettlement controversies.

sub_clusters.name: Fall of the Derg
sub_clusters.description: EPRDF coalition advances; Mengistu flees May 1991; EPRDF captures Addis Ababa; Eritrean independence follows.

960.name: EPRDF Era, Abiy Ahmed, and the Tigray War
960.description: Ethnic federalism under EPRDF; Meles Zenawi's development state; Abiy Ahmed's reforms and Nobel Peace Prize; Tigray War devastation.

sub_clusters.name: EPRDF and Ethnic Federalism
sub_clusters.description: Meles Zenawi establishes ethnic federal system; developmental state model; TPLF dominance; contested elections 2005.

sub_clusters.name: Meles Death and Transition
sub_clusters.description: Meles Zenawi dies 2012; Hailemariam Desalegn succeeds; Oromo and Amhara protests 2015-2018; state of emergency.

sub_clusters.name: Abiy Ahmed and Reforms
sub_clusters.description: Abiy Ahmed becomes PM April 2018; releases political prisoners; peace with Eritrea; Nobel Peace Prize 2019; Prosperity Party replaces EPRDF.

sub_clusters.name: Tigray War
sub_clusters.description: War erupts November 2020 between federal forces and TPLF; Eritrean involvement; mass atrocities; humanitarian catastrophe; Pretoria Agreement November 2022.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
